title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review
abstract: BackgroundGastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tongue-image analysis may provide an objective, low-cost, and non-invasive adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification.MethodsThis systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 principles and was informed by diagnostic test accuracy and prediction-model reporting frameworks. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception to 10 June 2026. Eligible studies were original investigations applying machine-learning or deep-learning methods to digital tongue images for gastric cancer, precancerous gastric lesions, or related gastrointestinal disorders and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric. Data were extracted on study design, sample size, target condition, reference standard, image-acquisition protocol, model architecture, validation strategy, diagnostic performance, calibration, interpretability, and risk of bias. A narrative synthesis was performed because of substantial heterogeneity.ResultsThe search identified 139 records, of which 78 remained after duplicate removal. After title, abstract, and full-text screening, 9 studies published between 2018 and 2025 were included. The evidence covered gastric cancer, precancerous gastric lesions or high-risk gastric screening, and related gastrointestinal disorders. Models included logistic regression and XGBoost classifiers based on handcrafted features, convolutional neural networks, transformer-based architectures, segmentation-assisted pipelines, and multimodal models combining tongue images with clinical, questionnaire, biomarker, or microbiome data. Internally validated AUCs ranged from 0.61 to 0.99 across target conditions. External validation was reported in only three studies and generally showed performance degradation, particularly for precancerous gastric lesions. Calibration assessment was uncommon, and most studies did not report calibration curves, Brier scores, expected calibration error, or recalibration procedures.ConclusionAI-based tongue-image analysis is a promising but early-stage approach for non-invasive gastric disease screening. Current evidence supports its potential role as an adjunctive pre-endoscopic triage tool rather than a replacement for gastroscopy. Prospective external validation, standardized image acquisition, transparent model reporting, calibration assessment, and evaluation in diverse populations are required before clinical deployment.Systematic review registrationhttps://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261444857, PROSPERO CRD420261444857.

title: Lipid-Protein Reciprocal Coupling: A Quantitative Analysis of Membrane Curvature, Architecture, and Protein Association
abstract: Cellular membranes are dynamic molecular landscapes in which lipid composition, transbilayer asymmetry, membrane curvature, thickness and mechanics collectively shape protein organization and function, while proteins can in turn remodel lipid organization and membrane architecture. Yet lipid-protein interactions are often treated as discrete binding events, obscuring the extent to which the physical organization of the membrane itself constitutes an active determinant of protein conformational states and cellular activity. Here, we investigate lipid-protein reciprocal coupling by integrating quantitative analyses of curvature-dependent protein-membrane association and hydrophobic-run organization with established structural, lipidomic and biochemical evidence. Our analysis reveals substantial variation in protein association with curved versus flat membrane environments and highlights how membrane curvature, together with lipid composition, cholesterol and asymmetry, can regulate protein structure and function, including in disease-associated systems. We further examine emerging lipid sensors, spatial proteomics and advanced biomimetic membrane platforms that are beginning to bridge molecular mechanisms with protein-lipid organization in cells. In particular, suspended membranes, pore-spanning systems and nanopillar architectures offer opportunities to independently control lipid composition, leaflet asymmetry, curvature and mechanics while directly interrogating protein behaviour. Together, these findings support a model in which membrane architecture encodes physical information that is read by proteins and reciprocally reshaped by protein activity to regulate cellular function.

title: Total Synthesis of Complex Nucleoside Antibiotics Ezomycin A1 and A2
abstract: The complex nucleoside antibiotics ezomycin A1 and A2 have stood as formidable synthetic challenges for half a century due to their density of polar functional groups and unique trans-fused bicyclic framework. Here, we disclose their long-awaited first total synthesis. This convergent and modular strategy is enabled by a stereoselective nickel-catalyzed reductive cross-coupling, a de novo asymmetric carbohydrate synthesis, and a mild (p-Tol)2SO/Tf2O-promoted N-glycosylation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mean First-Passage-Time-Directed Bias Optimization with Gaussian-Kernel Markov Models
abstract: Rare transitions limit the direct simulation of molecular kinetics and complicate the design of enhanced-sampling biases that accelerate specific events without obscuring their mechanism. We develop a data-driven framework in which biased trajectory data are combined using dynamic histogram analysis and represented by either conventional grids or normalized kernel-anchor memberships to construct finite row-stochastic kinetic models.

title: Microstate-Aware Excited-State Descriptors Improve Scaffold-Robust Prediction of Drug Phototoxicity
abstract: Drug phototoxicity depends on electronically excited states whose energies and intensities can change with protonation, tautomerism, and conformation, yet most predictive models represent a single parent structure. We evaluated a molecular-state-aware workflow on a curated 450-compound in vitro photoirritation (PIV) benchmark expanded to 1,088 microstates. Across 10 repeated 5-fold scaffold-held-out cross-validations, mean ROC-AUC increased from 0.745 for structure alone to 0.792 after adding parent xTB+sTDA descriptors, 0.807 with microstate summaries, and 0.808 with conformer aggregation…

title: A Novel Mononuclear Nickel Complex as a Precatalyst for Ionomer-Dependent Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity
abstract: In electrocatalytic water splitting, ionomer-catalyst interactions can significantly influence electrochemical performance. Molecular metal–organic complexes offer a tractable platform to investigate such interactions. Here we report a novel nickel–2methylimidazole complex, [Ni(2-MeIm)4(NO3)]NO3, with Ni@N4O2 coordination environment. The structure of this new material is established by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and supported by vibrational spectroscopy and thermal analysis.

title: An Epidemic of Misbranding: Marketplace Surveillance of MGM-15 and Kratom Alkaloids in Commercially Available Tablets by QuEChERS -LCMS/MS
abstract: The commercial kratom market increasingly includes concentrated and semi-synthetic products, including 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15), whose prevalence and concentration across the marketplace remain largely uncharacterized. Kratom alkaloids, namely mitragynine (MIT) and its diastereomers, share the same molecular formula and connectivity. The product ions commonly monitored are not structurally specific, further exacerbated by the semi-synthetic derivates.

title: Advances in Multiscale Computational Modeling of 2D Nanomaterials for Solar Cells: From Interface Design to Fabrication and Stability
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials provide a versatile platform for next-generation solar cells because their electronic structure, optical response, carrier transport, and interfacial chemistry can be engineered across multiple scales. However, photovoltaic performance and operational stability are governed not only by intrinsic material properties but also by coupled processes involving charge redistribution, interfacial recombination, ion migration, thermal transport, degradation, and fabrication-dependent microstructure.

title: Confinement-Driven Transient Coordination Complexes: H2 Dissociation and Quantum Channel Modification in Single-Atom Contacts
abstract: Understanding chemical reactivity at cryogenic temperatures is essential for advancing both fundamental quantum science and next-generation catalytic technologies. At the single-atom limit, geometric confinement can promote ground-state electronic effects that drive novel chemical events without thermal activation. Using the H2 interaction with transition-metal nanocontacts as a benchmark, we report the barrierless formation of a transient tip complex characterized by a diborane-like 4-electron, 3-center bond (Pt–H ~0.17 and 0.18 nm).

title: Accelerating the Discovery of Marine Natural Products with Antimicrobial activity via Bioactivity-Driven Molecular Networking
abstract: The growing threat of antimicrobial resistance underscores an urgent need to investigate underexplored natural sources to provide new chemical scaffolds for drug development. Marine environments, particularly those along the South African coastline, represent reservoirs of novel chemical diversity with the potential to provide new classes of antibiotics. This study reports the development of an efficient biodiscovery pipeline for the assembly and systematic screening of marine natural products extract libraries to identify novel antimicrobial leads.

title: Detection of Molecular Oxidation States in Dye Sensitized Solar Cells-Relevant Organic Dyes Eosin Y Through Optical UV/Vis Absorption Spectrum Changes
abstract: This study investigates oxidative degradation mechanisms of the non-metallic organic dye Eosin Y in order to examine precisely how they influence the light-harvesting efficiency (LHE) of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs). Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Time-Dependent DFT (TD-DFT) computations with ABINIT are used to construct the molecular geometry and electronic configuration of the dye in its neutral form, oxidized adduct state , and oxidized state with excited electron.

title: Coupled Field-Gated Nucleation and Autocatalytic Growth in Ferroelectric Switching
abstract: Polarization switching in fluorite (HfO2, Hf0.5Zr0.5O2) and wurtzite (AlScN) ferroelectrics is dispersive: nominally identical devices and domains switch over a spread of time rather than at a single threshold. The nucleation-limited-switching (NLS) model treats this phenomenon as a Lorentzian-in-log-time distribution of nucleation waiting times; Kolmogorov–Avrami–Ishibashi (KAI) theory instead treats switching as deterministic nucleation-and-growth.

title: Hydrogen-Bond-Induced Dual Structural Response in Amide-Functionalized Self-Assembled Monolayers
abstract: Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy reveal a dual structural response in N-(2-mercaptoethyl)heptanamide SAMs on Au(111). A persistent intermolecular hydrogen-bond network suppresses conformational fluctuations between the Au-S interface and the amide plane.

title: Thermodynamics and Accurate Solubilities of Lithium and Sodium Salts in Imidazolium-Based Ionic Liquids
abstract: Determining the solubility of metal salts in ionic liquids is challenging using visual methods or Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC). The slow crystallization kinetics of the metal salts impede accurate Solid-Liquid Equilibrium (SLE) measurements, resulting in significant discrepancies in the limited available literature. We propose Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) as an alternative technique to measure the solubility of metal salts in ionic liquids at different temperatures. Some new solubility data of lithium and sodium salts in imidazolium ionic liquid were determined.

title: Excited-State Photophysics Improves Scaffold-Robust Phototoxicity Prediction and Reveals Compound-Specific State Effects
abstract: Phototoxicity is controlled by light absorption and access to reactive excited states, but predictive models usually encode only a single ground-state structure. Here, a physically staged representation was evaluated on 450 compounds (192 positive, 258 negative) with 10 repeated five-fold scaffold-grouped cross-validations. Structure alone gave ROC-AUC 0.745 ± 0.018 and PR-AUC 0.668 ± 0.027.

title: Capturing the Effect of Exact Exchange in Thio-Michael Additions with a Machine-Learned Functional at Meta-GGA Cost
abstract: Semilocal density-functional approximations fail to describe the formation of anionic enolates in thio-Michael additions, the bond-forming step of covalent-inhibitor warheads; range-separated hybrids, which reintroduce long-range exact exchange, are required. Across the published CCSD(T)validated reaction pathways of eight warheads, we show that Skala—a deep-learned semilocal functional containing no exact exchange—matches the range-separated hybrid reference for the activation barriers, enolate geometries and relaxed reactant structures, outperforming the global hybrid B3LYP at meta-GGA…

title: Precision of Gaussian, Lorentzian, and pseudo-Voigt peak fitting under Gaussian noise
abstract: Discriminating subtle differences in measured signals is essential to scientific discovery. Knowledge of the attainable precision limits of fitted peak parameters and the physical and statistical factors that determine them provides a rational basis for improving this capability. However, without a common framework for comparing peak shapes and noise statistics, universal features of peak-parameter precision remain difficult to distinguish from those specific to a profile or noise regime, thereby hindering the development of general guidance for peak fitting and measurement design.

title: Coherent Recrossing Challenges Mechanistic Interpretations from Surface Hopping
abstract: Surface hopping is widely used to assign mechanisms in ultrafast molecular photodynamics, yet the resulting mechanistic picture can become strongly method-dependent when electronic coherence survives across recurrent nonadiabatic interactions. We identify this regime, which can arise in dense excited-state manifolds, as coherent recrossing. Using semiclassical analysis of the prototypical Tully dual avoided-crossing model, we disentangle three controlling ingredients: phase accumulation between nonadiabatic events, electronic decoherence, and the relative phase information encoded in the…

title: Access to Broad Organosulfur Chemical Space by Iron MHAT Sulfinamidation of Olefins
abstract: Organosulfur groups, particularly in the S(VI) oxidation state, have seen increased adoption within the medicinal chemistry community in recent years. Although certain groups such as sulfones and sulfonamides have been utilized since the advent of modern drug development, others like sulfonimidamides or sulfoximines have only recently seen utilization. These desirable functionalities provide access to new chemical space and intellectual property while enabling the optimization of key ADME properties.

title: Health risk assessment of carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic heavy metal exposure from commercial instant noodles in Bangladesh: a deterministic and probabilistic evaluation for adults and children
abstract: The contribution of the instant noodle cake itself to dietary heavy metal exposure in Bangladesh has not been quantified. Nine metals (Pb, Cd, Cr, Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, Ni and Co) were determined by flame atomic absorption spectrometry in eight leading brands (102 packets) from Dhaka, Rajshahi and Khulna, seasoning sachet excluded. The hazard index (HI) and total cancer risk (TCR) were estimated for adults and children at national-average (0.36 g day -1 ) and high-consumption (25.6 g day -1 ) ingestion rates, with uncertainty propagated by bootstrap Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Assigning the Low-Energy Excitons in Far-Red Photosystem II through Atomistic Modeling
abstract: Far-red light photoacclimation of cyanobacteria extends the spectral range of oxygenic photosynthesis through the incorporation of chlorophylls (Chls) d and f into natural Photosystems, but the energetic organization of these pigments remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electronic-structure calculations with atomistic QM/MM and polarizable QM/MM approaches to determine the site energies, electronic couplings, and excitonic structure of the far-red PSII from Synechococcus sp. PCC 7335.

title: Testing for the presence of Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals in Locally Available Perfumes in Pakistan Through GC-MS Analysis and Implications for Public Health Policy
abstract: Introduction Many conventional perfumes contain Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs) like phthalates, synthetic musk, and parabens – often hidden under the ingredient label ‘fragrance’ or ‘parfum.’ Daily exposure to EDCs, through inhalation and skin contact, is very harmful, resulting in multiple health issues in infants, children, and adolescents undergoing critical developmental stages. In Pakistan, consumers remain considerably unaware, making this a serious problem. Perfumes are typically produced by unauthorised local manufacturers who do not follow standard protocols.

title: Comprehensive Quantum Chemical Interaction Analysis of Whole Protein–Ligand Structures in BindingDB Using the Fragment Molecular Orbital Method
abstract: Understanding protein–ligand interactions based on their electronic states is important for elucidating molecular recognition and supporting structure-based drug discovery. In this study, we performed fragment molecular orbital (FMO) calculations, a quantum chemical approach, for a comprehensive set of experimentally determined protein–ligand complexes derived from BindingDB.

title: Direct Access to α-Chiral Amino-Oxetanes via Boron-Assisted Aziridine Ring-Opening
abstract: α-Chiral amino-oxetanes represent a high-value yet synthetically difficult to access scaffold class in medicinal chemistry, combining the favorable pharmacokinetic properties of the oxetane ring with an additional degree of molecular complexity and three-dimensionality. Here we report the first synthetic route to α-chiral amino-oxetanes bearing boron and silicon substituents via a boron-assisted aziridine ring-opening strategy.

title: Playing Domino with Carbon: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Methanol with Cobalt Phthalocyanine
abstract: Electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide to methanol represents one of the most demanding transformations in CO 2 conversion, requiring the management of a six-electron, six-proton sequence while suppressing competing pathways toward carbon monoxide, formate, and hydrogen evolution. Among molecular electrocatalysts, cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) has emerged as a unique molecular platform capable of extending CO 2 reduction beyond CO through a domino-like cascade of protoncoupled electron transfer steps.

title: Scientific World Models: Toward Closed-Loop Scientific Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from task-specific scientific tools toward foundation models, generative design, research agents, and autonomous laboratories. Despite this progress, most systems remain organized around isolated predictions or local workflows. They rarely maintain an evolving account of scientific objects, predict the consequences of interventions, or learn systematically from computational and experimental evidence. This article introduces scientific world models as a core paradigm for closed-loop scientific intelligence.

title: In-column Synthesis and Atomic-resolution Electron Microscopic Analysis of Metastable Reactive Nitrides
abstract: Metastable and air-sensitive compounds are challenging to synthesize and characterize because their formation often requires harsh conditions and their structures can rapidly evolve upon exposure to the environment. Here, we demonstrate that a high-vacuum environment inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) column can serve simultaneously as a reaction platform and an atomic-scale analytical tool for generating and interrogating such materials.

title: PervoTransformer: Multi-Scale Transformer-Based Device Design and Atomistic Modeling of Perovskites
abstract: Perovskite solar cell design involves a large and highly coupled space of material compositions, layer structures, and physical parameters, making systematic exploration of complete device architectures computationally challenging. This work introduces PervoTransformer, a transformer-based framework that represents complete device architectures as sequences and learns device-level behavior directly from this representation. A RoBERTa model is fine-tuned on SCAPS-generated device sequences spanning six perovskite families, including MAPbI3, FAPbI3, CsPbI3, and their Sn-based analogs.

title: Product Accelerated Photodegradation of Nitro-Spirothiopyrans
abstract: The long term stability of conjugated fluorescent and photochromic compounds is essential for their application in materials and devices, but is often highly sensitive to changes in molecular structure. This aspect is particularly prominent in the 6'-nitro-spiropyran and 6'-nitro-spirothiopyran photochromes, which differ only in a O/S atom at the spiro center but show remarkably different stability under UV irradiation.

title: Enantioselective Strain-Release Formal (3 + 3) Cycloaddition of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to Chiral 1,4-Diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Relay Dy/Ir Catalysis
abstract: *Email: nowmiracle@zjnu.edu.cn; dengwp827@zjnu.edu.cn ABSTRACT: Pyrazines and piperazines are privileged 1,4-diaza motifs, yet neither combines conformational rigidity with a stereochemically defined three-dimensional shape. Here we report the first catalytic enantioselective formal (3 + 3) cycloaddition of 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), providing direct access to enantioenriched 1,4diazabicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes—rigid, C(sp3)-rich scaffolds that serve as chiral three-dimensional complements to these classical motifs.

title: Impact of Structural Water on Ionic Conductivity in Hydridoborates Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Sodium closo-hydridoborates have emerged as promising solid-state electrolytes for Na-ion batteries because of their high ionic conductivity and electrochemical stability. However, their sensitivity to water makes them challenging to scale-up. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of controlled hydration on the structure, ion transport, and interfacial stability of an anion-mixed hydridoborate, Na4(B10H10)0.5(B12H12)0.5.

title: Establishing Optical-Spin Interfaces in Luminescent Organic Diradicals using Spin-selective Symmetry-breaking Charge Transfer
abstract: Luminescent organic diradicals based on tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM) radicals have shown promise as optical-spin interfaces important for quantum sensing. The optically driven spin polarization mechanisms of existing TTM diradicals remain limited by non-selective singlet-triplet intersystem crossing (ISC) pathways, which restrict optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. Two TTM-based diradicals were prepared in which the two TTM subunits are linked at the para positions of one of their phenyls.

title: Ring-Conformer Ensembles Improve AutoDock Vina Docking; an Ant Colony Makes Them Affordable
abstract: In standard preparation, AutoDock Vina holds five-and six-membered non-aromatic rings at their input pucker, and our failure analysis of 4 509 runs against searchreachable native poses shows what that costs: with the accurate preset, the search itself fails in only 6.5% of runs, while ring conformations, ranking and the scoring function account for most of the rest.

title: From prediction to process control: a critical review of machine learning in reactive dyeing of cotton
abstract: Abstract Reactive exhaust dyeing of cotton uses large amounts of water, salt, alkali and heat, partly because the recipe and programme are fixed when a batch starts. This review asks whether learned models, acting on the machine during a batch, have been shown to reduce that consumption. An OpenAlex search (2003 to September 2026, 862 records) and web searching identified 27 primary studies of learned, rule-based, model-based or search-based methods, or inline monitoring, in reactive dyeing of cotton. Each was coded by setting and by how far its output reached the process.

title: Non-Covalent Interactions Directed Azobenzene Crystals: Photoisomerization-Induced Melting and Melt-Mediated Polymorphism
abstract: Azobenzene molecular crystals have emerged as a compelling class of stimuli-responsive materials, yet the structural factors that determine whether a given crystal bends, melts, or remains entirely inert under UV irradiation are far from understood.
